scenes.headline: What is Apache Spark?
scenes.subtitle: A unified engine for large-scale, distributed data processing.
scenes.narration: Apache Spark is a unified, open-source engine that processes very large datasets in parallel across a cluster of machines.

scenes.headline: Why Spark exists
items: A single machine runs out of memory and CPU on big data
Spark spreads the work across many machines at once
It keeps data in memory to avoid slow disk round-trips
One API covers batch, SQL, streaming, and machine learning
scenes.narration: A single machine runs out of resources on large data, so Spark spreads the work across many machines. It keeps data in memory to avoid slow disk trips, and one unified API covers batch, SQL, streaming, and machine learning.

scenes.headline: How a Spark job flows
scenes.narration: You write ordinary-looking code, and the driver turns it into an optimized plan. That plan is split into tasks that executors run in parallel, and the results come back to you.

scenes.headline: A first Spark program
scenes.code:
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession

spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("Intro").getOrCreate()
df = spark.read.json("s3://bucket/logs/*.json")
df.filter(df.status == "ERROR").groupBy("service").count().show()
scenes.narration: We create a SparkSession, then read a folder of JSON logs into a DataFrame. We filter for errors, group by service, count them, and call show to trigger the job. Nothing actually runs until that final action.

scenes.text: Spark makes distributed data feel like local code — but it only runs when you call an action.
scenes.narration: The key idea is that Spark makes distributed processing feel like ordinary local code, yet nothing executes until you trigger an action.
